mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.25% compresses the risk-free rate, reducing equity discount rates and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.25% (p-value < 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate rise above 0.5% in a 3-month window signals monetary tightening, increasing equity discount rates and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of triggered instances (FEDFUNDS > 0.5% for 3 months).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate and increase in nonfarm payrolls signals strong labor market conditions, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction between UNRATE decline and PAYEMS growth fails to predict positive 60-day returns (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, high consumer credit (RSAFS > 450 billion) and rising housing starts (HOUST > 1.2 million) signal robust household spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion regimes (RSAFS > 450 billion and HOUST > 1.2 million), S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases (p-value < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in unemployment rate indicates improving labor market conditions, increasing household income and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE is declining (p-value < 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts falling below 1.1 million units in a 3-month window signals housing sector contraction, reducing consumer wealth and corporate revenue, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of triggered instances (HOUST < 1100 for 3 months).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production and quarterly GDP growth signals broad economic contraction driven by supply shocks, reducing corporate earnings and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when INDPRO < 106 and GDPC1 < 16300, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 235), a federal funds rate rise above 0.5% signals aggressive monetary tightening, increasing borrowing costs and reducing equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when CPIAUCSL > 235 and FEDFUNDS > 0.5, S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns).
